_readme: Reference facts for the Apollo 15 simulator. Split into two groups: FLOWN_HARDWARE (what Apollo 15 actually used in 1971 — cited to the Apollo 15 Mission Report and contemporaneous NASA engineering documents) and MODERN_COMPARISON (today's ISS-era NASA-STD-3001 standards, shown only for contrast — they did not exist in 1971 and never governed this mission). An earlier version of this file applied modern ISS thresholds (cabin CO2/O2/pressure limits, a daily exercise-compliance regimen) directly to Apollo hardware; that was a mismatch and has been corrected here — see README 'Corrections' section.

cabin_atmosphere.value: 100% oxygen, nominal 5.0 psia (34.5 kPa); emergency floor 3.5 psia (24.1 kPa)
cabin_atmosphere.note: Apollo CM and LM both used a pure-oxygen, low-pressure cabin — not the nitrogen/oxygen mix and ~14.7 psia used on the ISS today. Launch-day atmosphere was a mixed sea-level-pressure gas, bled down to 5 psia pure O2 during ascent/early translunar coast (a post-Apollo-1 safety change).
cabin_atmosphere.source: Biomedical Results of Apollo (NASA SP-368), Ch. "Command and Service Module Environmental Control System"; NASA feature '50th Anniversary of NASA Deciding on a Mixed-Gas Atmosphere for Apollo'

co2_removal.value: Lithium hydroxide (LiOH) canisters, no automated ppCO2 alarm threshold used in this app
co2_removal.note: Apollo used disposable LiOH canisters, not the ISS's regenerable CDRA system. No continuous cabin-CO2 telemetry for Apollo 15 was located in the sources used to build this prototype, so this app does not chart a CO2 trend for this mission — it states the real removal method as context instead of inventing numbers.
co2_removal.source: General Apollo ECS documentation (NASA SP-368); this app does not extend beyond what was sourced

biosensors.value: ECG (heart rate) and impedance pneumogram (respiration rate) only
biosensors.note: No pulse oximetry (SpO2) and no continuous skin-temperature telemetry existed in the 1971 bioharness — both are anachronistic for this mission and were removed from this app's Vitals panel accordingly.
biosensors.source: Apollo 15 Mission Report, Section 10.1 (Biomedical Instrumentation and Physiological Data)

food.value: ~2,800 kcal/day planned; actual average intake 2,801 (CDR) / 2,372 (CMP) / 2,568 (LMP) kcal/day

radiation.value: Net integrated dose 360 millirad (CDR), 510 millirad (LMP); passive dosimeter average 300 millirad at skin depth — well below thresholds for detectable medical effect

bone_mineral.value: Measured ~4% loss in radius bone mineral content, attributable to weightlessness; both crewmen back to baseline within 2 weeks postflight
bone_mineral.note: This is a real measured result from the M-078 experiment (pre/post-flight X-ray densitometry), not a continuous in-flight measurement or a model — Apollo 15 was 12.3 days, too short and not instrumented for in-flight bone-loss tracking the way long-duration ISS missions are.
bone_mineral.source: Apollo 15 Mission Report, Section 10.4 (Bone Mineral Measurement)

exercise_countermeasures.value: None flown as a daily countermeasure regimen
exercise_countermeasures.note: The ISS's ~2.5h/day, 6-days/week aerobic + resistance exercise protocol is a post-Apollo (Skylab-onward) countermeasure developed once missions got long enough for cardiovascular/musculoskeletal deconditioning to matter. Applying it to a 12-day Apollo mission would be anachronistic, so this app's Activity panel tracks real EVA metabolic workload instead of an exercise-compliance percentage.
exercise_countermeasures.source: General spaceflight-medicine literature (Ploutz-Snyder, NASA JSC ISS exercise Rx); absence for Apollo confirmed by the lack of any such program in the Apollo 15 Mission Report

heart_rate_bpm.note: General clinical resting range, era-independent. EVA-period elevation above this range is expected exertion, not an alert — see 'eva_context' below.

vitals_general_reference.source: General clinical reference ranges, not mission- or era-specific.

eva_context_rule: A heart-rate or respiration reading during a logged EVA window is not flagged, however high, because elevated rate from physical exertion during a moonwalk is expected and healthy — the real 1971 concern was Irwin's EKG RHYTHM (paired beats with pauses), not his rate, which is why this app treats the cardiac arrhythmia as a distinct scripted medical event rather than something a simple rate threshold could have caught. A rate-only monitor would have missed exactly the thing that mattered — see README.

modern_comparison._readme: For contrast only — none of the following governed Apollo 15. Included so the app can show how far astronaut health monitoring has moved on since 1971.
modern_comparison.cabin_atmosphere_iss: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6003, V2 6006]: ~14.2-14.9 psia total pressure, 145-155 mmHg O2 partial pressure, two-gas (N2/O2) mix.
modern_comparison.co2_limit_iss: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004]: average 1-hour ppCO2 <= 3.0 mmHg; OCHMO-TB-004.
modern_comparison.exercise_iss: ~2.5 h/day, 6 days/week aerobic + resistance exercise (Ploutz-Snyder, ISS ExRx; Smith SM et al., 2012).
modern_comparison.sleep_iss: Scheduled 8.5 h/night; observed spaceflight average ~5.96-6.09 h (Barger LK et al., Lancet Neurology, 2014) — notably, sleep deprivation was already a real problem in 1971 on Apollo 15, as this mission's own sleep-displacement data shows.
